scenes.title:
Turn a script into
motion cards
scenes.lead: JSON owns the content. HTML and CSS own the visual system. GSAP owns rhythm. FFmpeg owns delivery.
scenes.caption: Generate a 16:9 HTML composition, then render it to MP4.

scenes.title: What changed in this version
scenes.lead: Content, style, timing and output path are now controlled by data and flags.

cards.title: JSON driven
cards.body: Edit data/demo-video.json instead of hand-editing HTML every time.

cards.title: Style selectable
cards.body: Choose from Bauhaus, Art Deco, Pop Art, Y2K and more.

cards.title: Audio aware
cards.body: When audio is passed in, ffprobe reads duration and the visuals are rebuilt to match.

scenes.caption: The workflow stays local, simple and friendly to coding agents.

scenes.title: From script to video

steps.title: Write script
steps.body: Put titles, cards, captions, steps and metrics in JSON.

steps.title: Pick style
steps.body: Use --style to switch between 16 visual systems.

steps.title: Build HTML
steps.body: Generate a 1920 by 1080 composition and render metadata.

steps.title: Mux MP4
steps.body: HyperFrames renders visuals. FFmpeg combines audio and video.

scenes.caption: Visual duration can come from JSON or from the audio file.

scenes.title: More expressive card videos
scenes.lead: The visual grammar borrows from the social card style system and adds motion layers for video.
scenes.caption: Style switches affect color, type, border, texture, shapes and motion tone.

scenes.title: Edit text, switch style, add audio, reuse
scenes.lead: This is now an extensible skeleton for card-video production.
scenes.caption: Next layers can include TTS, batch rendering and publishing workflows.
